card.title: Plant breeding and SCP — yield plus protein

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Food security stacks four strategies: plant breeding (selection → hybridisation → superior recombinants, e.g. high-yield rust-resistant wheat), single-cell protein (Spirulina/yeast biomass as cheap protein), scientific animal husbandry (breed selection, feed, disease management — Gir/Sahiwal cattle, Leghorn poultry), and biofertilizers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, mycorrhiza, cyanobacteria) that fix or free nutrients sustainably.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: breeding pipeline: germplasm → selection → hybridisation → evaluation → release  ·  SCP: microbes (Spirulina, Methylophilus) = 50–70% protein biomass  ·  biofertilizers: Rhizobium (legume nodules) · Azotobacter (free-living N-fixer) · mycorrhiza (P uptake) · BGA/cyanobacteria (paddy)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: New varieties need multi-location trials (G×E interaction) before release. SCP needs sterile cheap substrate plus safety clearance (nucleic-acid limits). Biofertilizers need compatible host/soil (Rhizobium is legume-specific). Animal gains need feed + health + housing together — genetics alone underdelivers.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Green Revolution wheats (semi-dwarf, fertilizer-responsive) tripled yields — and taught input-dependence. Spirulina ponds turn wastewater-adjacent culture into protein. Apiculture/sericulture/pisciculture diversify farm income beyond crops and dairy.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Design a breeding answer: objective (rust resistance + yield) → collect germplasm → cross resistant × high-yield parents → select recombinants over generations → multilocation trials → release. Each step earns its line; the pipeline order itself is frequently the question.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: High-yield varieties often trade taste/nutrition and demand water/fertiliser (sustainability tension). SCP faces acceptance + nucleic-acid concerns. Biofertilizers act slowly and variably — supplements, not substitutes, at scale. Monoculture invites epidemics (Irish-blight lesson).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From heterosis: F1 hybrids outyield parents (dominance/overdominance models), but segregate in F2 — hence hybrid seed repurchase yearly, the economics inside the biology. SCP math: microbial doubling in hours vs crops in months — exponential growth is the protein argument.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Four pillars chant: breeding–SCP–husbandry–biofertilizers, one example each. Breeding steps in order (5 words: collect–cross–select–trial–release). N-fixers: Rhizobium (nodules), Azotobacter (free), BGA (paddy).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: plant-breeding steps with one released-variety example; SCP definition with two sources; biofertilizer types with host specificity; dairy/poultry breed + management triad.
